recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Superheroes as a modern pantheon", "body": "Chance opens by arguing that Eternals is an ideal first film for the series, since its godlike immortals are said to inspire every culture's gods and goddesses. Citing Chris Knowles' Our Gods Wear Spandex, he says modern culture has turned from traditional pantheons toward worshiping Captain America, Spider-Man, Superman and Batman on the silver screen. He traces darker heroes to the Spider-Man issue where Gwen Stacy dies, and flags Ikaris, a Superman-style hero who becomes the villain. Gabe adds that learning Jack Parsons' birth name was Marvel convinced him these stories weave reality and fiction while keeping ancient archetypes alive."}, {"title": "The hidden hand in plain sight", "body": "Gabe reads the yod, the Hebrew letter for hand and the number ten, as a signature running through the film, from Napoleon's hand in his shirt to the 'have a nice day' delivery scene in The Matrix. He decodes MCU and MK Ultra as matching in a septenary cipher, and argues that the giant Celestial hand rising from a volcano, shot in the Canary Islands years before the La Palma eruption, reads as foreshadowing. Chance agrees that the Eternals, as secret gods steering humanity, fit the hidden hand idea, and the hosts treat the rose petals, blue skin signage and family crest as nods to dragon court bloodlines."}, {"title": "Kabbalah and the ten Eternals", "body": "Noting that ten Eternals arrive at the start of the film, Gabe places each one on the Kabbalistic Tree of Life. He puts Thena at the center for Athena's wisdom, her owl and its 360 degree view, which he links to the strega and strategy, sets Makkari at Hod, Kingo at Netzach beneath Ikaris, Druig at Malkuth as the foundation stone, and Sprite at Kether. He also walks through the Pythagorean tetractys and a diagram of ten concentric rings. Chance adds a reading of the name Arishem, with ari as lion in Hebrew and shem as a name of renown, casting the Celestial as a Yaldabaoth style demiurge."}, {"title": "Evolution, war and the cosmic egg", "body": "Chance explains the backstory, in which Arishem seeds planets with Celestials that hatch like cosmic eggs once enough intelligent life exists, and Gordy points out that Galactus also gestated in an egg. Chance notes Sersi greeting the Charles Darwin statue and a theme where Deviants evolve while the Eternals cannot, and says their directive not to interfere in human conflict frames war as the engine of evolution. He hears alchemy in Dane's line about a seed of perfection at the heart of the earth, and asks whether the plan to put a god to sleep hints that ascension could be dangerous, while the group links the Eternals' Uni-Mind to Zardoz."}, {"title": "Old myths behind new heroes", "body": "The hosts trace nearly every Eternal to older stories. Gabe reads the first Deviant as Echidna, mother of monsters, Chance casts Thena as Enkidu to Gilgamesh, and Gordy spots an ammonite in Sersi's classroom and a Kronos echo in the corn Gilgamesh chews for his drink from the Battle of Troy, which the group reads as communion. Ikaris is read as a solar Christ figure recast as Judas, and Chance reads Makkari's sign language as the silent code of a priest class. The group links Phastos' plow to Ursa Major before Sprite's light show, then plays with the Ebony Blade's Latin inscription read backwards."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Chance launches Marvelous Demystifiers, a monthly movie club, with Gabe (Slick Dissident) and later Gordy to decode the symbolism in Marvel's Eternals. They read the film's Celestials, Eternals and Deviants through Kabbalah, Greek and Babylonian myth, the hidden hand and the sky clock, including Gabe's view that the Canary Islands finale foreshadowed the La Palma eruption.
fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "The elites are using these childhood stories to weave reality and fiction, and for that matter also to keep very ancient stories alive so that we don't forget.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The Eternals in this film and from the original comics are characters that are said to be basically godlike, immortal, and that their presence on Earth is what inspires the idea of gods and goddesses.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "So when I watched this movie, I could not stop thinking that this movie, which was made years before La Palma, was foreshadowing the La Palma event.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Athena has the owl, has 360 degree perspective because it can spin its head in all directions, and that's where strega and strategy are very much in correspondence.", "author": "Gabe (Slick Dissident)", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/794d3a0b-c42b-4791-84c3-f79eff430f4c/SLICK-DISSIDENT.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "The son of God is the sun.
